title: Programming recall
learner: Returning learners who have seen programming but need to recover stepwise execution and debugging habits.
assumedKnowledge: Basic function notation; no installed programming environment required

include: Debugging with evidence and boundary tests
exclude: A full Python or C++ course, environment installation, arbitrary code execution, recursion, object-oriented design, file/network access, concurrent programs, pointer or memory management

conventions: Original snippets use Python 3, integer arithmetic unless otherwise labeled, four-space indentation and explicit inputs.
Lists supply indexed collection practice; they are not presented as C++ arrays. Python division, dynamic binding and list behavior must not be transferred blindly to C++.
Answer fields ask for values and reasoned choices, not arbitrary source-code evaluation. Activities trace bounded built-in programs.

routes.quick: Use four diagnostic probes, then Quick recall and every independent checkpoint. Finish the four-part mixed check.
routes.full: Study values and decisions, loops and indexing, functions and shared data, then debugging and tests. Predict before stepping through programs.

overlap: F01 arithmetic and precedence support expression evaluation.
F03 mathematical functions support input/output language but program state and side effects need explicit distinctions.
The baseline has no committed CSC 242/252 lesson pack or reusable programming family.
reuse.implementation: Reuse rational/choice fields, deterministic generator and independent checkpoint APIs, lesson reader, notes, resume and backup. Add only scoped families and a bounded trace activity.

assessment.checkpoints: Four critical multipart questions per lesson cover all listed subskills, with no more than eight fields per question.
assessment.mixed: One multipart question per lesson. Lesson checkpoints retain complete structural coverage.
assessment.evidence: Familiarity, visits, guided traces and assisted practice remain separate from independent F10 objective evidence.

sharedCapabilities.interface: MathText recognizes fenced Python code and inline backtick code inside existing string fields, renders escaped semantic code with preserved whitespace and keyboard-scrollable blocks.
sharedCapabilities.integration: No saved-attempt or question schema change. Existing math outside code is unchanged; fenced strings retain indentation. Add focused rendering/escaping checks.
One union member and reader dispatch. Scoped component predicts before stepping through pure bounded trace models; no eval, new storage or full interpreter.

verification: Independently execute generated Python snippets with an available Python runtime and compare expected fields; also use separate arithmetic/loop/list oracles for 100 seeds per structure.
Test empty/singleton lists, both step directions, excluded endpoints, equality thresholds, negative floor division, alias/copy behavior, missing returns, invalid indices and numerical tolerances.
Check code indentation and escaping in prompts, examples and feedback, complete objective coverage and deterministic seeds.
Exercise all four guided traces/activities, diagnostic routing, independent checkpoints, resume, notes, backup, keyboard, desktop/mobile Axe and screenshots; full test/lint/type/build.
Only then mark preview, record human review pending, push and begin F11 detailed planning.
